title: Qt: add byte annotations and offset markers in hex view
description:
## Summary

- Add colored byte-range annotations with comments in the Qt hex view
- Keep annotations visible over field highlight
- Add offset markers (start/end byte) with compute dialog
- Compute offsets relative to protocol ranges, with exception for TCP segment data/payload
- Session-only annotations (no persistence in this MR)
- Comment length is limited to 256 characters
- Annotations are cleared before capture changes to avoid cross-capture display

## Why 

This helps analyze unknown/proprietary protocols that don’t have a dissector in Wireshark by allowing users to mark and measure byte ranges directly in payloads.

## Demo Video:

 https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GIh8kl_TtxPIZaKEaODvtaBh9v8AeKZ3/view?usp=drive_link (old video, now without save annotation session-only)

## Testing

- cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
- tools/checkAPIs.pl ui/qt/data_source_tab.cpp ui/qt/widgets/hex_data_source_view.cpp
  - Warning: Found shadow variable(s) in ui/qt/data_source_tab.cpp : index
- Manual: add/edit/remove annotations, hover tooltips, offset markers on protocol fields and TCP segment data, change capture (annotations cleared), restart Wireshark (annotations not saved, expected)

AI-Assisted: yes (OpenAI Codex)

notes.body: I like the idea of this MR, but I'm not sure I like saving the annotations in a file at the same path as the existing file plus added extensions.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23373/diffs?diff_id=1645802162&start_sha=8d36f55999f4175e5db35f766fee809211a0d4e6#df01c4e761b3d81227312e4c5612ee1dd4c17d7b_321_329)

There's a lot of ways in which the path of the existing file plus an extension might not be writable. It might be a temporary file from a live capture. (Your text under saveAnnotations seems to assume that a temporary unsaved file has a null `!cap_file_->filename`, but that is not correct, it has the temporary file name.) It might be on a read-only partition or remote network drive. It might be a shared file that multiple people access. It might be a pipe or FIFO. Always popping up a warning message upon opening a file where the annotations file could not be written seems like a problem.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23373/diffs?diff_id=1645802162&start_sha=8d36f55999f4175e5db35f766fee809211a0d4e6#df01c4e761b3d81227312e4c5612ee1dd4c17d7b_341_343)

I think a better approach for saving annotations is similar to that done by adding comments or time shifts, etc., where it marks the file as having unsaved information, has the data changed in memory, and writes it out later, which would avoid popping up warning messages until someone tried to save.

(The requests in #19919 and #19682 ask for a way to save packet markings in pcapng at the record level rather than bytes, but are somewhat related and this would help with that.)
It might make more sense to save annotations in a file (or files, or files in a directory) in the user profile directory, and then possibly develop a way for pcapng to hold the annotations directly.

Only profile related files shall be saved in the profiles directory, so storing annotations here is a no-go. We will eventually add support for nested profiles which will use directories here.

I will suggest looking at an pcapng option to store annotations in a generic way, not limited to the hex view only. Having this in separate files will not work and it's almost impossible to share a pcapng file with annotations.
It might be reasonable to get the base functionality in the graphic highlighting first and handle how to save them later.

@johnthacker @stigbjorlykke

Thanks for the feedback. Given the concerns about sidecar files and that the profiles directory must not be used for this, I agree it’s best to split this work. I’ll update this MR to focus on the base UI functionality (byte-range highlighting + comments + tooltips + offset markers) with annotations stored in-memory for the current session only, and defer persistence to a follow-up once we agree on the proper storage mechanism (likely pcapng-level support). This avoids any writeability/shared/tempfile issues and removes popup warnings during open. Does that split sound acceptable?
